thesis: The speaker describes his early academic focus on China as a contrarian choice when Japan was the dominant market, leading him to study economics to assess China's future rather than its past. He recounts teaching Western economics in China during the open-door policy era, where students were instructed that Marxism-Leninism was the correct economics, yet they displayed a sophisticated, three-dimensional political awareness and intense curiosity about the subject.
